concerns: The Indonesian answer denotes a general head covering, while the Malaysian answer specifically denotes a garment hood.
response.cue_rationale: A concise cue rewrite would either broaden the concept to “head covering,” which changes the intended hood sense, or retain “hood,” which makes “tudung kepala” insufficiently precise.
material_concerns: The pair may teach a category-versus-subtype mismatch: “tudung kepala” need not be attached to clothing, unlike “hud”.

preference_risk.rationale: The shorter “tudung” may compete with “tudung kepala,” but the larger issue is that Indonesian usage is broader than the specific garment-hood sense.

response.rationale: The proposed forms do not reliably express the same exact clothing sense. “Hud” is a hood, whereas “tudung kepala” is broader and can refer to a head covering generally.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: No relevant shared synonym concern was identified beyond the underlying sense mismatch.
